items.title: The Nepal floods seem a world away – but make no mistake, climate breakdown will affect us all | Nesrine Malik
items.summary_raw:
Richer countries might have more resources to deal with catastrophe, but this problem grips the entire planet, however much leaders may want to deny it

Climate breakdown is happening on one Earth, but two different worlds. In one, its impacts increasingly encroach on everyday life; longer periods of discomfort and shorter periods of sharp pain. Endless, hotter summers, and within them sudden wildfires, evacuations, homes burned to cinders in a matter of hours. In another, catastrophe. This summer has been a snapshot of that split-screen. The hottest day on record in parts of Europe, and a wave of water, mud and ice in Nepal that so far has claimed more than 750 lives. Thousands of people are still missing.

The difference is also one of resources. The climate crisis has an economic cost, but some places can absorb it better than others. The three frameworks seek to establish a unified and coherent approach to land-use planning, with clear rules for investment and stronger safeguards for the environment and local communities. In a statement to the Athens-Macedonian News Agency (ANA-MPA), Minister of Environment and Energy Stavros Papastavrou said: “with the three Special Spatial Planning Frameworks for Industry and the Supply Chain, Renewable Energy Sources and Tourism, we are completing a major reform that Greece has needed for years. We are organizing land use and leaving behind the fragmentation and inertia of decades. At the center of an exclusive report by The Telegraph is the ultra-luxury casino resort City of Dreams Mediterranean. According to the report, the hotel’s facilities, particularly its upper floors, could be used as an observation point overlooking the British base, according to intelligence and military sources cited by The Telegraph. A representative of City of Dreams Mediterranean categorically rejected the claims, stressing that the property operates exclusively as a tourism and business resort. The report points to the geographical location and height of the 16-story hotel, which have reportedly raised concerns among security officials and RAF personnel. With certain observation equipment, it would potentially be possible to monitor aircraft takeoffs and landings, as well as the movements of officials and military personnel.

items.title: Dead and Missing After Ship Carrying 267 Passengers and Crew Capsizes Off Kyrenia
items.summary_raw:
NICOSIA – A passenger vessel carrying 259 people and eight crew members capsized off the coast of Kyrenia around midday Sunday, August 30  as a rescue operation involving the Turkish-occupied north’s so called coast guard and civil defense teams was underway. According to the illegal Turkish Cypriot Bayrak broadcaster, the passenger catamaran was traveling to the port of Tasucu in Mersin, southern Turkey. The high-speed passenger vessel, operated by Filo Denizcilik, departed from Kyrenia’s tourist harbor and, while several kilometers offshore, began taking on water at the bow. According to available information, the captain attempted to return to port but was unable to do so. The vessel quickly began listing and eventually capsized. The so-called prime minister of the Turkish-occupied north, Unal Ustel, announced that 237 of the 267 people aboard had been rescued, seven were recovered dead and 23 remained missing.

items.title: Araghchi calls for accountability over US use of Japan's airbase to attack Iran
items.summary_raw:
Araghchi calls for accountability over US use of Japan's airbase to attack Iran

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has called on the Japanese public to hold their government accountable over reports that US military assets stationed in Japan were used in operations against Iran.

Speaking to Kyodo News, Araghchi referred to reports that US Air Force F-16 fighter jets deployed from Misawa Air Base to the Middle East took part in operations against Iran.

“The peace-loving people of Japan should ask their government to be held accountable for the crimes committed by the United States,” Araghchi said, arguing that Tokyo bears responsibility for how military facilities and capabilities based in Japan are used.

Greece is set to sign a $3.6 billion defence deal with Israel on Monday in Tel Aviv, which will provide Athens with an air defence system.

The project, known in Greece as “Achilles Shield”, will become the largest defence export deal in Israel's history, according to Jerusalem Post.

Most of the funds will go to Rafael Advanced Defense Systems, which will supply Greece with David's Sling systems designed to intercept heavy rockets and ballistic missiles, as well as mobile SPYDER systems designed to counter unmanned aerial vehicles and drones, the report said.

Israel Aerospace Industries will provide the Barak MX system, which is designed to defend against aircraft and missiles.

items.title: The U.S. has transferred large quantities of missiles and air-defense systems to the Middle East for the Iran war, leaving some stockpiles in Europe and Asia at critically low leve…
items.summary_raw: The U.S. has transferred large quantities of missiles and air-defense systems to the Middle East for the Iran war, leaving some stockpiles in Europe and Asia at critically low levels, according to U.S. officials.  Patriot, ATACMS and other precision weapons have been heavily depleted, while THAAD interceptors and counterdrone systems have also been shifted to the region. Replenishing inventories could take years.  The shortages are forcing U.S. commanders to adjust contingency plans and have raised concerns about Washington’s ability to respond simultaneously to a potential Chinese attack on Taiwan or a Russian threat to NATO.  Source: WSJ

All our efforts are for the establishment of alliance and unity. All our endeavors are for building an atmosphere of peace and security in our region. More than 400 endangered animal and plant species could face accelerated extinction after the Donald Trump administration’s decision to rescind a rule that has protected old-growth forests for more than two decades.

According to a new report from the Center for Biological Diversity, the rollback of the Bill Clinton-era “roadless rule” could put 7.4m acres (3m hectares) of endangered-species habitat and nearly 1,800 miles (2,900km) of protected rivers and streams at risk, while opening more than 45m acres of national forests to roads, drilling and logging.

items.title: Trump Administration Starts Building Border Wall Project in Arizona Over Tribe’s Objections
items.summary_raw:
PHOENIX (AP) — The Trump administration has begun work on a project to build a stretch of border wall in southern Arizona along part of a Native American tribe’s reservation, pushing ahead with one of its signature projects despite protests from the tribe. U.S. Customs and Border Protection says the area is a dangerous smuggling route and that building the wall will close a longstanding security gap. But members of the Tohono O'odham Nation, whose membership spans both sides of the U.S.-Mexico border, have accused the administration of trespassing and say the construction will damage land sacred to the tribe. The wall segment is part of a $46 billion effort by the Trump administration to fill the border with 30-foot (9-meter) steel bollard walls, vehicle barriers, and technology designed to stop undocumented immigration and smuggling.

The post Trump Administration Starts Building Border Wall Project in Arizona Over Tribe’s Objections appeared first on The National Herald.

A series of strong El Niño climatic patterns in recent decades, such as the “Godzilla” event currently brewing that is set to warp weather around the world, have been supercharged by the broader overheating of the planet caused by the burning of fossil fuels, a major new study has found.

El Niño is a naturally occurring phenomenon, taking place every two to seven years, when the waters of the eastern tropical Pacific Ocean heat up, causing a cascade of impacts around the world. The latest developing El Niño, set to peak later this year, is set to be the strongest in living memory and has been informally dubbed a “Godzilla” event.

items.title: The Guardian view on the Nepal-Tibet floods: prepare for more climate-linked disasters | Editorial
items.summary_raw:
Medicine, food and other supplies are the urgent priority. But the rising risks from shrinking glaciers must be faced too

Thousands of people in Nepal and Tibet are in desperate need of emergency assistance following Wednesday’s disaster. With 360 people confirmed dead, more than 1,300 others are still missing as search and rescue operations continue. The precise sequence of events linking glacier collapse to flash floods is yet to be confirmed. But there is no doubting the enormous destructive power of the brown torrent that can be seen on video clips surging down the steeply sided Himalayan valleys, sweeping away everyone and everything in its path.

Testimony from survivors about terrifying near-escapes and losses is reminiscent of previous disasters, including the 2004 tsunami. The human cost among the less well off will be more people regularly choosing whether to skip meals, ignore other bills or stay cold this winter.

items.title: Germany's far-right AfD pledged to remove refugee and disabled children from mainstream schools if it wins the Saxony-Anhalt regional election on September 6.  The party's manifest…
items.summary_raw: Germany's far-right AfD pledged to remove refugee and disabled children from mainstream schools if it wins the Saxony-Anhalt regional election on September 6.  The party's manifesto calls the "inclusion experiment failed" and says refugee children should be educated separately "to reinforce the message that their stay in Germany is only temporary."   Islamic education would not be offered as "Islam is not part of Germany."  The AfD also plans to expand Russian language teaching and reinstate school exchanges with Russia, citing cultural ties from the East German era.  The AfD leads polls heading into the election.   It would need over 40% to form the first wholly AfD government in German history.

items.title: Iran’s nuclear chief says attacked nuclear sites not secure for IAEA inspection
items.summary_raw:
Iran’s nuclear chief says attacked nuclear sites not secure for IAEA inspection

Iran’s nuclear chief Mohammad Eslami said on Wednesday that the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) would not be able to inspect the country's nuclear sites that have suffered attacks in recent months until it develops a specific inspection protocol for such sites and their security is ensured, adding that Iran is still in a wartime situation, in comments carried by Iran’s IRNA news agency.

Eslami said that Trump's threats to bomb the alleged secret Iranian nuclear site show the IAEA are pawns of the US and Israel, and accused the countries of pressuring the IAEA for an inspection.

items.title: Trump Has Submitted Civil Nuclear Agreement With Saudi Arabia to Congress for Review
items.summary_raw: WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump has submitted to Congress for review an agreement with Saudi Arabia aimed at bolstering the kingdom's civilian nuclear program, but continues to insist that it won't move forward if Saudi Arabia doesn't normalize relations with Israel, according to a Trump administration official. The classified document was submitted to Capitol Hill on Monday as required by the Atomic Energy Act, according to the administration official, a congressional aide, and two others familiar with the matter. All four spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to comment publicly on the classified matter. The agreement was signedlast month in Washington by U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright and his Saudi counterpart. But the next day, Trump announced he was requiring the Saudis to normalize relations with Israel through the Abraham Accords as part of the pact — raising doubts that the agreement would come to fruition. Neither the administration official nor the others familiar with the matter would comment on whether Trump's call for the Saudis to join the accords is detailed in the classified document submitted for the congressional review.<

items.title: Groups sue Trump’s EPA over fast-track approval of toxic datacenter chemicals
items.summary_raw:
Exposure to two compounds approved can result in ‘sudden death’ and range of other serious health risks, lawsuit warns

The Trump administration has approved two new datacenter chemicals to which exposure can result in “sudden death” and a range of other serious health risks, like cancer, eye corrosion, neurological damage and reproductive harm, a new lawsuit warns.

The two compounds approved by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) for import and immediate use in facilities across the US are photoacid generators that also appear to be Pfas “forever chemicals”, though it is unclear because much of the EPA documents are redacted. Some Pfas are commonly used in the production of semiconductors.

This article was amended on 26 August 2026. A previous version said the EPA concedes that the chemicals present an “unreasonable risk” to workers. It has been updated to say the chemicals may present an unreasonable risk.

items.title: France is pushing to limit Ukraine's ability to buy non-European military equipment with EU loan money, seeking to steer the €60 billion defense portion of the EU's €90 billion sup…
items.summary_raw: France is pushing to limit Ukraine's ability to buy non-European military equipment with EU loan money, seeking to steer the €60 billion defense portion of the EU's €90 billion support package toward European and French producers.  Ukraine has secured two exemptions so far: one for Chinese drone components and another for US Patriot interceptor missiles.   France wants these exemptions to be temporary, with European suppliers replacing foreign ones as production ramps up.  Nine EU countries including Germany, Sweden, and Poland pushed back, calling for Ukraine to have "maximum flexibility to procure the equipment it urgently needs."  France has a clear commercial interest: its Franco-Italian SAMP/T system is Europe's closest alternative to the US Patriot.  Source: Euronews

The war has crippled Qatar’s LNG lifeline, with damage at Ras Laffan and severe disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz. Qatar is reported to have lost roughly $24 billion in gas sales during the major disruption.

Doha has responded with deep budget cuts, cutting some government spending by 30% and overseas aid by roughly 85%.

Israel's far-right national security minister, Itamar Ben Gvir, posted a video of himself sitting at what he said was the director’s desk of Unrwa in Qalandiya Refugee Camp, celebrating the raid on the UN agency. 

On Tuesday, Israeli forces stormed Unrwa vocational centres in Qalandiya and Kufr Aqab that serve about 16,000 Palestinian refugees across the occupied West Bank.

"On my shift there is no Unrwa, no management, they will not be here."

Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said in a televised interview on Tuesday that the Strait of Hormuz remains closed despite a temporary transit agreement with Oman.

“America and other countries should know that the Strait of Hormuz will not be opened except through Iranian arrangements,” Gharibabadi said, adding that Iran remains “in a state of war”.

Gharibabadi says Iran and Oman have held talks over the past 40 days on a transit arrangement through the waterway, agreeing on a temporary route seven miles (11 kilometres) wide, with the entry point and part of the exit route running through Iranian territorial waters.

items.title: Israel is planning to expand its military capabilities in space, including eventually striking targets on Earth from orbit.  Defense Minister Israel Katz says Israel wants to be fi…
items.summary_raw: Israel is planning to expand its military capabilities in space, including eventually striking targets on Earth from orbit.  Defense Minister Israel Katz says Israel wants to be first to develop a true space-to-ground attack capability. The broader plan also includes better satellites, encrypted communications, cyberwarfare and missile defense.  One concept discussed is the U.S. “Rods from God” idea: satellites dropping massive tungsten rods at extreme speed, producing bunker-busting impacts without nuclear explosives. The physics are possible, but cost, weight and effectiveness remain major obstacles.  Israel is considering roughly 16 billion shekels ($5.4 billion) in space investment over a decade, though funding is not yet assured.  Source: Haaretz

The climate damage caused by developing the Rosebank and Jackdaw oil and gas fields under consideration by the UK government would destroy their economic benefits many times over, according to an analysis.

It estimates the economic damage caused by the carbon pollution from the oil and gas produced would be between £119bn and £336bn in the coming decades, compared with the £28.7bn in value to the UK estimated by Adura, the fossil fuel company promoting the new fields.

The ministry accused the two lawmakers of having “consistently acted against Israel”, including by calling for international legal proceedings against Israelis.

It also accused them of spreading “false accusations against Israel”, including allegations of genocide, deliberate starvation and the intentional targeting of children and medical personnel.

items.summary_raw:
Average sea surface temperature outside polar regions was 21.1C on Saturday, latest data finds

The world’s oceans were hotter than ever previously recorded on Saturday, according to the latest data.

The average surface temperature was 21.1C, with the rising marine heat a stark indicator of the climate crisis. More than 90% of the heat trapped by carbon dioxide from fossil fuel burning enters the oceans.

items.title: This is not a natural calamity: it is being done to us knowingly
items.summary_raw:
Global heating is an outrage, not a tragedy. We deserve the facts about the climate crisis – I choose the Guardian because it’s one of the few places left to share them honestly

  • Climate campaign 2026: help us reach 30,000 acts of support

Well, there’s no getting around it now. What many of us once feared has become a reality.

The dangerous conditions climate scientists long warned of have become our common, if deeply unwelcome, experience, and season by season, our acquaintance with disorder and extremities deepens. In both hemispheres, wildfires rage right into our cities and incinerate entire neighbourhoods. Marine heatwaves are bleaching corals and cooking seagrasses on a global scale. This northern summer has brought temperatures most Europeans associate with the Australian desert. Heat events in Europe have paralysed whole countries, destroyed infrastructure and killed citizens in their thousands.

The technology could also be used in semi-solid and solid-state batteries in the future.

items.summary_raw:
Carbon capture and storage could make the Rosebank site compatible with UK net zero commitments – if its owners are willing to pay the price

The British government must soon decide whether it should give consent to two oil and gasfields, Rosebank in the North Atlantic and Jackdaw in the North Sea. Amid both insecurity of energy supplies and deadly evidence of the climate crisis, the prime minister, Andy Burnham, is facing pressure from the oil and gas industry and unions on one side, and environmentalists on the other.

Labour’s manifesto commitment not to approve new drilling licences offers little help, because the fields already have licences, granted by the previous Conservative government in 2022 and 2023. But last year, Edinburgh’s court of session ruled that the environmental impact assessments on which this decision relied were unlawful. The largest share, $48 million, is intended for charging infrastructure for electric cars, while commercial vehicles, hydrogen refuelling and workforce training will also receive support.
